absent: Physical and mapped sizing algorithm and validation of skip offsets and part lengths.
Mixing permutation definitions and numeric initial constants for wide and narrow states.
Key object layouts and key-length requirements for full and reduced digests.
Internal sorter algorithm, ordering guarantees, and callback contracts.
Depot hash function, record layout, pool sizing, and handle-to-record translation.
Freelist reuse policy, grace-cookie checking, and persistent versus refcounted paths.
Spare pool slot purpose and pool array lifetime management.
Concurrency rules for depot lookup and statistics beyond stated guards.

findings.text: Scatter list splitter partitions one input chain into several output chains based on a byte skip and a table of part lengths. It allocates transient splitter records and per-part output arrays, derives both physical and optionally mapped views, publishes output pointers and mapped counts, and releases temporaries on success or all partial output on failure.

Keyed 64-bit digest interface offers generic buffer entry points for aligned and unaligned input plus fixed-arity helpers for one to four wide words and for one and three narrow words. All share a common key type and length-aware framing, differing only in how message words are supplied.

Reduced-round 32-bit digest family with wide internal state provides aligned and unaligned buffer entry points plus helpers for one to four narrow inputs. Multi-word inputs pack pairs into wider blocks before mixing, and short tails merge into the length block.

Compact narrow-state digest family provides aligned and unaligned buffer entry points plus helpers for one to four narrow inputs, processing small blocks one word at a time with single mixing rounds and a distinct result derivation.

Processor identity helpers return the current processor number while validating that the caller cannot migrate. One reports misuse for generic identity queries, another specializes the report for per-CPU accessors.

Generic array sort front ends accept a base pointer, element count and width plus comparison and exchange callbacks. Two variants thread an opaque caller context through reentrant callbacks, while a third adapts legacy callbacks without context; each selects atomic or caller-managed scheduling behavior.

Stack-trace depot lifecycle and handle services include early-init request, early and late table initialization, handle-to-record lookup, reference release, and packing of small side bits into handles alongside bit extraction.

Full digest framing initializes four lanes from distinct constants, folds two key words into the lanes, and seeds an accumulator with the message length in the top byte. Finalization mixes that accumulator, applies two mixing rounds, re-mixes, marks a domain byte, then applies four more rounds before combining lanes into the wide result.

Buffer hashing consumes full eight-byte little-endian blocks with two mixing rounds per block, then merges any trailing few bytes into the length accumulator. Aligned and unaligned variants differ only in load helpers; one build path pads the tail with a masked load while other builds assemble the tail by width-specific loads.

Fixed-arity helpers encode their total input byte count in framing and mix each supplied wide word with two rounds, except single narrow input and the trailing word of the three-narrow form which merge directly into the accumulator after packing the first pair into one wider block.

First reduced family reuses wide framing and a single-round mixing primitive. Per-block mixing uses one round, finalization uses one round before domain marking and three after, and the narrow result truncates the same four-lane combination used by the full digest.

Second reduced family uses narrow lanes and accumulator with length in the top byte, a dedicated narrow mixing primitive, four-byte block iteration with one round per block, narrow tail assembly for up to three bytes, and a final result formed from only two lanes after one plus three final rounds.

Splitting first sizes outputs from the physical view, materializes physical partitions, and only then re-sizes and materializes the mapped view when a mapped count was supplied. Publication of output pointers and mapped counts happens after both views complete.

Hash sizing honors an explicit bucket order when set, otherwise derives entry count from free memory scaled by a table factor, then clamps into a fixed order interval. Early allocation uses early hash and block allocators; late allocation uses generic zeroed allocators and records mask as entries minus one.
Handles embed a small side field alongside identity; setting bits on an empty handle yields empty rather than storing, and extraction returns only the side field without affecting identity.

Sort core dispatch uses small integer sentinel callback values to select optimized exchange paths for wide words, narrow words, byte-wise moves, or a wrapper that adapts legacy callbacks, with a zero sentinel selecting wrapper comparison.

Late table initialization serializes one-time setup under a function-local mutex, rechecking disabled and already-initialized states after acquiring it and releasing on every path including allocation failures.

Reference-count release path asserts the pool guard is not held, then takes it with interrupt state saved while deferring console output. Hash unlink, grace-cookie capture, freelist append and statistics updates all occur under that guard.

Misuse reporting disables preemption without tracing, brackets diagnostics with instrumentation guards, and restores preemption without rescheduling, avoiding recursion while emitting rate-limited diagnostics and a stack dump.

Sort adapter record carries a legacy comparison callback together with a legacy exchange callback, allowing the generic reentrant core to invoke non-reentrant caller functions through a shared private pointer.

Depot maintains a small fixed set of long statistics covering refcounted allocation, release and in-use populations plus freelist depth and persistent entry count and bytes, each paired with a stable display name for diagnostics.

File-local depot state comprises a hash bucket array, bucket-order and mask values, a pool pointer array with pool count and spare pool slot, a disabled flag, an early-init passed flag, and a capped maximum pool count.

Depot moves from uninitialized to early-initialized or disabled during early boot exactly once, then optionally to late-initialized on first use. Disabled state short-circuits both initializers and lookups, allocation failure forces disabled, and early request after the early pass warns.

Splitter lifecycle proceeds through helper allocation, physical sizing, per-part output allocation, physical materialization, optional mapped re-sizing and materialization, publication, and helper release; any sizing or allocation failure diverts to a cleanup state freeing all per-part outputs and helpers before returning an error.

Processor-id validation returns immediately when preemption is already accounted, interrupts are masked, caller is a per-CPU thread, migration is disabled, or boot has not reached scheduling; otherwise it emits a diagnostic and then returns the sampled identifier.

Reentrant sorts forward caller callbacks and privacy pointer plus an atomicity selector to a shared internal sorter; the legacy adapter builds a short-lived wrapper record and forwards wrapper sentinels with non-atomic behavior.

Boot parameters toggle depot disablement via boolean parsing and tune maximum pool count with range checks that retain the prior value on error. A late debug entry exposes pool and counter statistics as text when the depot is enabled.

Transient helper exhaustion, physical or mapped sizing failure, or any per-part output allocation failure yields a negative error after freeing prior partial outputs; mapped processing is skipped entirely when no mapped count is supplied.

Diagnostics are rate-limited and include caller address and stack dump; recursion is avoided by masking preemption during reporting, and the function still returns a sampled identifier even on the misuse path.

Empty handles yield null records and are ignored by release and bit-setting paths. Release of a handle that no longer resolves warns and returns without touching reference state; only a final decrement triggers reclamation.

Reclamation cannot sleep or re-enter the depot, so it avoids blocking grace waits and deferred callbacks, instead recording a grace cookie and queueing on a freelist tail ordered oldest-first to preserve concurrent traversal safety.
Hash table scale is 14, minimum bucket order 12, maximum 20, and hash seed is 0x9747b28c.
Device control bits occupy position 30 for clock gating and position 31 for soft reset.
Exchange selector sentinels are 0 for wide-word moves, 1 for narrow-word moves, 2 for byte moves and 3 for wrapper dispatch; comparison wrapper sentinel is 0.
Default maximum pool count is 8192 capped by pool-index width; boot tuning rejects values below 1024 or above that width maximum, and depot log lines carry a fixed textual prefix.
